rfm_tuples.R: Tax Receivable Agreement (TRA) liability: 'At December 31, 2024, such obligations with respect to previously consummated transactions totaled $20.4 million ... Future payments ... are expected to be substantial.' Related-party: 'Of these amounts, $5.6 million is payable to Fertitta Family Entities.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — derive whether the TRA is an under-disclosed related-party liability. Each future LLC Unit exchange triggers a step-up that obligates RRR to pay 85% of the tax saving to the pre-IPO holders (mostly Fertitta family). With 45.99M LLC Units still outstanding, the contingent TRA could be 10-20x the disclosed $20.4M.
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (10-K Note 14 Related Party + Item 1A risk factor on TRA)
rfm_tuples.M_value: 10-K discloses TRA liability of $20.4M on the balance sheet AND clearly states future exchanges 'are expected to be substantial.' Risk factor explicitly: 'In certain cases, payments to the Fertitta Family Entities under the tax receivable agreement may be accelerated or significantly exceed the actual benefits we realize in respect of the tax attributes subject to the tax receivable agreement.' 45.99M LLC Units held by NCI (almost entirely Fertitta family) remain exchangeable — RRR settled only ~900k units' worth in FY2024. The contingent TRA exposure on remaining units could plausibly be $200-400M at full exchange (rough scale-up from disclosed $20.4M for ~58% already converted).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B catch — the $20.4M on the balance sheet is technically correct, but it understates the structural Fertitta-family transfer engine baked into the corporate structure. Each exchange triggers a step-up the family captures 85% of. The disclosure is honest (the risk factor language is clear) but a non-specialist reader could underweight this. This is the same kind of UPC tax-shield structure that has hurt other dual-class issuers when exchanges accelerate. Watch-list.

summary: RRR is a structurally well-disclosed controlled company with strong Mode A integrity: clean Big-4 auditor (EY 10y), no going-concern, no material weakness, no Item 9 disagreements, no covenant trips, no Wells notices. The smoking-gun Mode B signal cuts FOR the company, not against: the Fertitta brothers (90% voting power) made ~$20.6M of open-market PURCHASES in August 2024 at $49-$55, while the only insider sales were modest CFO/President vest-and-sell patterns. The May 2024 'S' on Frank Fertitta's filings is a footnoted intra-family estate-planning trust transfer, not a sell-of-conviction. Mild Mode B catches: (1) Q1 2025 ADR/RevPAR/F&B all softened 4-7% YoY while 10-K and Q1 10-Q narratives keep saying 'favorable customer trends' — disclosed in the numbers, not in the prose; (2) 2025 capex guidance + dividends imply a ~$150-200M funding gap (special dividend was quietly skipped); (3) Mono tribe advances now $102M and growing, unsecured/subordinated. None of these are concealment — they are visible in the filings — but they suggest the -20% pre-cutoff drawdown reflects a real Las Vegas locals consumer softening that management is narratively reluctant to acknowledge.
